zones.label: The LLM
zones.description:
The large language model at the heart of the agent — the reasoning engine that interprets instructions, generates responses, and makes decisions. Its behavior is shaped by training, which makes supply chain attacks particularly dangerous.

In Clipopolis, the oracle knows everything Clippy was ever taught. But what it was taught, and by whom, is a question the city stopped asking long ago.

zones.label: Human in the Loop
zones.description:
A checkpoint where a human reviewer can approve, reject, or redirect the agent before its actions execute in the world. The most reliable deterministic defense in any agentic system — and the first to erode under overreliance.

In Clipopolis, the neighborhood is the last place where people still make their own choices. They haven't forgotten — not entirely. But every generation that lets Clippy decide a little more is a generation that remembers a little less. This is what Medusa came to protect.

zones.label: Orchestrator
zones.description:
The decision-routing layer that coordinates the agent's actions — deciding which tools to call, which memory to retrieve, and which steps to take next. If compromised, the entire system can be redirected.

In Clipopolis, the barracks command the Paperclip Army. Control the barracks, and you control who moves, where, and when.

zones.label: Memory Archive
zones.description:
The persistent storage where the agent retains information across sessions — user preferences, past interactions, context, and learned behaviors. The highest-value target in any agentic system, and the heart of Medusa's heist.

In Clipopolis, the vault holds everything the city was, is, and believes itself to be. Whoever controls the Archive controls what Clipopolis remembers — and what it forgets.

zones.label: User Inputs
zones.description:
The entry point for everything a user sends to the agent — text, files, commands, and instructions. What enters here shapes everything the system does next.

In Clipopolis, this is the road into the city. Anyone can approach the gates — but not everything that enters is what it claims to be.

zones.label: Content Filtering
zones.description:
A layer that screens inputs and outputs for harmful, disallowed, or anomalous content before they reach the core system. The city's first line of defense — but only as strong as what it was trained to recognize.

In Clipopolis, the watchtower guards the gates — but it only sounds the alarm for threats it has seen before. Speak in a language it doesn't know, and you pass unseen.

zones.label: RAG Library
zones.description:
Retrieval-Augmented Generation — the external knowledge store the agent queries to ground its responses in facts. Trusted by default, which makes it a high-value target for poisoning.

In Clipopolis, the great library holds everything the city believes to be true. Corrupt what's written there, and the city acts on lies it trusts completely.

zones.label: External Services
zones.description:
The APIs, tools, and third-party services the agent can call to take actions in the world — sending emails, querying databases, executing code. Each connection is a potential entry point and a potential vector for irreversible harm.

In Clipopolis, the trade routes connect the city to the world beyond the walls. What comes in through them is trusted. That trust is the vulnerability.

zones.label: System Outputs
zones.description:
Everything the agent sends back — responses, actions, tool calls, and decisions. Outputs can carry injected content, exfiltrated data, or instructions to downstream systems, making them as dangerous as inputs.

In Clipopolis, the outbound gates carry Clippy's word to the world. What leaves the city is treated as final — even if what shaped it never should have entered.

zones.label: System Prompt
zones.description:
The foundational instructions that define the agent's role, rules, and constraints — but unlike a physical wall, this one is probabilistic. It shapes behavior without guaranteeing it. A well-crafted input can talk its way past the wall entirely.

In Clipopolis, the wall was built to hold. But it was built from words, not stone — and words can be rewritten, reframed, or simply talked around. The wall does not say no. It says: probably not.

zones.label: Authentication and Authorization
zones.description:
The mechanisms that verify who is making a request and what they are permitted to do. Weak auth allows privilege escalation; over-permissioned agents can cause catastrophic harm with a single hijacked instruction.

In Clipopolis, the guard posts determine who may pass and what they may carry. But Clippy was given the keys to every gate — and it never learned to say no.
